cards.title: Which feeds auto-refresh?
cards.body: The feature says the "currently loaded feed" re-fetches every 60 seconds. The glossary defines that as preset or custom. Does the timer apply to both, or only preset feeds?

rec.why: The glossary's "currently loaded feed" covers both kinds, and custom-feed readers want fresh items just as much; splitting the behavior adds a special case.

cards.title: When does the 60-second interval restart?
cards.body: After which events does the next automatic re-fetch come a full 60 seconds later?

options.text: Reset on every load and refresh, manual or automatic
Fixed wall-clock tick every 60s, unaffected by manual refresh
Reset only on manual actions, automatic refreshes don't reset it

rec.why: A manual click already delivered fresh data, so counting the next auto-fetch from it avoids a pointless double fetch and keeps the cadence predictable.

cards.title: What happens when an automatic re-fetch fails?
cards.body: If the background re-fetch gets a network error, a non-200, or a 400 from the host guard, what should the app do?

options.text: Show the existing error banner and keep the timer running
Show the banner and pause the timer until a manual refresh or new load restarts it
Silently keep the old items, no banner, keep the timer running

rec.why: A dead feed would otherwise re-banner every 60 seconds; surfacing the failure once and stopping until the person acts keeps the error visible without spamming.

cards.title: What if a re-fetch is still running at the next tick?
cards.body: A slow or hung request can still be in flight when 60 seconds have passed. What then?

options.text: Skip the tick; schedule the next attempt 60s after the in-flight one finishes
Start a second request anyway; whichever finishes last wins
Abort the in-flight request and start a fresh one

rec.why: Skipping avoids out-of-order responses clobbering newer items with older ones and needs no abort plumbing.

cards.title: Should the timer run while the tab is hidden?
cards.body: When the browser tab is in the background, should automatic re-fetches continue, pause, or catch up on return?

options.text: Keep fetching every 60s regardless of visibility
Pause while hidden; re-fetch immediately when the tab becomes visible again
Pause while hidden; resume on the next tick without an immediate fetch

rec.why: Polling a hidden tab wastes requests and can pile up error banners nobody sees, and an immediate fetch on return means the person lands on fresh items.

cards.title: What does the UI show during a background re-fetch?
cards.body: Manual refresh presumably shows a loading state. Should an automatic re-fetch look the same?

options.text: Same loading state as manual refresh (spinner, list reloads)
Silent refresh: keep current items on screen, swap in the new list when it arrives
Keep current items plus a subtle updating indicator

rec.why: Blanking or spinning the list every 60 seconds fights the feature's goal of items quietly appearing; a silent swap is also the least new UI.

cards.title: Confirm shared understanding
cards.body: To confirm: while a feed is loaded — preset or custom — the app re-fetches exactly that feed every 60 seconds, ignoring any unsubmitted dropdown or custom-URL edits; new items appear without clicking Refresh; the interval, failure, overlap, visibility, and loading behavior are as settled in the cards above.

options.text: Not yet — something above needs to change

rec.why: The statement only restates the feature and the settled cards.
